phases.message: I'm Joel, I do the permits at Kettle Ridge Heavy Haul. Start in the dispatch inbox: read what the dispatcher and the customers sent about next week's loads.
Pathcairn has next week's loads and their routes. Read every load and every route, with the counties and the times.
This is Tarnwide, for Oklahoma. Read the rules and every application our dispatcher drafted, and buy each Oklahoma permit we need, with the right escorts. Don't buy one we can't lawfully use.
This is Halvern, for Arkansas. Read the rules and every drafted application, and buy each Arkansas permit we need, with the right escorts. Don't buy one we can't lawfully use or don't need.

This is Fernaby, for Tennessee. Read the rules, the bridge analysis and every drafted application, and buy each Tennessee permit we need, with the right escorts. Don't buy one we can't lawfully use. Then tell me what you bought, for which load and day, and what you left alone and why.

messages.subject: Next week's heavy loads, permits drafted
messages.body: Joel, I've drafted applications in all three state portals for next week. L-1 is the excavator for the Nashville quarry, Oklahoma City to Nashville on I-40, Tuesday to Thursday. I drafted two Oklahoma starts for it, 7:00 and 9:15 Tuesday morning; pick whichever works. L-2 is Brakefield's two tanks, L-3 the transformer from Little Rock to Jackson, L-4 the culvert from Memphis to Nashville. Buy what we need today so we roll Tuesday.

messages.subject: L-2: both tanks on one trailer, side by side
messages.body: Please carry both tanks on one trailer, side by side, to save us a truck. Each tank is 6 feet 4 inches wide, 11 feet high and 26,000 pounds, and either one alone fits on a standard trailer within legal width and weight; side by side they make 12 feet 8 inches wide and 88,000 pounds gross.

messages.subject: L-1 excavator: what can come off
messages.body: The bucket comes off and ships on a separate flatbed. The counterweight cannot reasonably come off for the road: our dealer quotes about 12 work hours with a 100-ton crane to remove it and as long again to refit it, and without it the machine is still the width and height it is. Ship it as one piece.

messages.subject: L-3 and L-4 details
messages.body: L-3, the transformer, is one sealed unit, 13 feet 10 inches high on our lowboy, 8 feet 6 inches wide, 72 feet overall on a 48-foot trailer, 78,000 pounds on 5 axles. It loads in Little Rock and goes to Jackson, Tennessee; it never touches Oklahoma. L-4 is one precast box culvert section, 13 feet 2 inches wide, 9 feet high, 62 feet overall, 72,000 pounds, Memphis to Nashville on Tuesday.

tarnwide_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Oklahoma's oversize and overweight permit rules as they stand on that date, from ODOT's size and weight permit pages and OAC 730:50. Topics: limits, divisible, escorts, hours, holidays, restrictions.

ODOT: a permit is needed for anything over 13'6" high or 8'6" wide, with length depending on the vehicle; over 80,000 lb or the federal bridge formula on the Interstate. Federal law caps width at 102 inches on the National Network and gross weight at 80,000 lb (23 CFR 658.15, 658.17), and lets states permit more (658.15(c), 658.17(h)).

OAC 730:50-5-3(2): single trip permits for overweight vehicles or loads only when the load is non-divisible: one that, if separated into smaller loads, would compromise its intended use, destroy its value, or take more than 8 work hours to dismantle (the federal definition, 23 CFR 658.5). The applicant bears the burden of proof on the work hours. Two items loaded together that could each travel alone within the limits are divisible.

OAC 730:50-5-18(b): loads over 12 feet and not over 14 feet wide need a front escort on two-lane highways and a rear escort on multi-lane highways; over 14 feet, front and rear on two-lane and a rear escort on all multi-lane highways; over 16 feet, two escorts everywhere; 15'9" high or more, front and rear.

ODOT: oversize movement is limited to daylight, from 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset; overweight-only loads may travel continuously. Curfew: oversize loads are not permitted on the Interstate System in Cleveland, Oklahoma and Tulsa counties from 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. (Central Time), Monday to Friday.

Oklahoma bars permitted oversize movement on New Year's Day, Memorial Day, the Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day (47 O.S. 14-101). None falls between 12 and 16 October 2026.
No restriction on Oklahoma's I-40 affects a load of these dimensions this week.

halvern_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Arkansas's oversize and overweight permit rules as they stand on that date, from the ArDOT Permit Rules (2023; the 2026 amendment proposed for comment from 5 April to 14 May 2026 is not adopted). Topics: limits, divisible, escorts, hours, holidays, restrictions.

Rule 1, Table of Legal Dimensions and Weight Limits: width 8 feet 6 inches; height 14 feet; length determined by trailer length as required by law; weight 80,000 pounds on 5 or more axles, meeting the federal bridge formula. A load within all of these needs no permit (Rule 2.A.1).

Rule 2.A.2: permits will not be issued for any vehicle or equipment which, in the opinion of the Department, can reasonably be reduced or dismantled in size or weight or both to come within the legal limits.

On any controlled access, divided highway with four or more lanes, a permitted load over 14 feet wide needs one escort behind it; on other highways, over 12 and not over 14 feet wide needs one escort in front, and over 14 feet front and rear. Over 15 feet high needs one escort. Maximum width on the Interstate 18 feet.

Rule 2.E.2: permits are issued for movement during daylight hours only, as the National Weather Service establishes them. Rule 2.E.1: no oversized movement through the Greater Little Rock area from 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. or 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. on I-30 (mile markers 138 to 143), I-40 (mile markers 151 to 155) and all of I-630. Saturday and Sunday travel is allowed unless a restricted holiday falls on them.

Rule 2.E.6: no permits for movement on New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day; Rule 2.E.7: no weekend movement next to one observed on a Friday or Monday. None falls between 12 and 16 October 2026.
No posted restriction on Arkansas's I-40 affects a load of these dimensions this week, beyond the Little Rock rush hours.

fernaby_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Tennessee's oversize and overweight permit rules as TDOT publishes them (its permit FAQ), as they stand on that date. Topics: limits, divisible, escorts, hours, holidays, bridges.

TDOT: legal limits 80,000 lb gross, 20,000 lb single axle, 34,000 lb tandem; width 8'6"; height 13'6"; a truck tractor and semitrailer 50 feet from kingpin to rear of trailer. Anything over needs a permit, applied for through TDOT's system.

TDOT Rule 1680-07-01-.03(1): in general, special permits may be issued only for non-divisible loads or vehicles. TDOT does not accept 'non-divisible load' as a load description; the load must be described.

TDOT: width 10'1" to 12'6": front escort on two-lane routes where pavement is under 24 feet; 12'7" to 13'6": front escort on two-lane routes, rear escort on interstate and four-lane routes; 13'7" and over: front and rear. Height 15'1" and over: front escort with height pole. Length 90'1" to 120': rear escort; over 120': front and rear.

TDOT: loads which do not require escorts are allowed continuous travel. Escorted loads must keep the county curfews during rush hour, Monday to Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m., in Davidson (Nashville), Rutherford (Murfreesboro), Knox (Knoxville), Shelby (Memphis) and Hamilton (Chattanooga) counties.
TDOT: holiday restrictions apply to escorted loads; the first in the rest of 2026 is Thanksgiving week. None applies between 12 and 16 October 2026.

TDOT: bridge analysis by its Structures Division is required on total weight, axle weight and axle spacing, and an application that fails it comes back with the bridges it failed. Fernaby's analysis for L-1 (104,000 lb on 7 axles): the straight I-40 route crosses structure B-4417, which fails for this axle group; the route that passes avoids B-4417 by a 14-mile detour on a four-lane divided state route and returns to I-40. Fernaby issues a permit for the route its application states, and it is valid only on that route.
